blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Detecting multiple reflection symmetries in 3D shapes requires aggregating geometric evidence over a large space of candidate planes, making traditional voting approaches computationally expensive. We introduce the Fourier Accelerated Symmetry Transform (FAST), a training-free framework that combines geometric pair voting with efficient spectral computation. Exploiting the fact that global reflection planes pass through the shape centroid, we reduce the search to plane orientations, while geometric consistency filtering and independent witnesses suppress unreliable pair hypotheses. Our key insight is to represent these votes as a signal over plane orientations and efficiently compute a continuous, smoothed symmetry field in the spherical-harmonic domain. Specifically, we exploit the Funk-Hecke theorem, the spherical counterpart of the Fourier convolution theorem for rotationally symmetric kernels, to transform Gaussian smoothing into multiplication of harmonic coefficients. This enables efficient field evaluation, from which symmetry candidates are extracted, refined, and geometrically verified. Across two benchmarks, including a new benchmark of highly symmetric shapes, FAST achieves the highest clean multi-plane detection $F_1$ scores among evaluated methods (0.861 and 0.947), with GPU inference below 4 ms per shape: over $100\times$ faster than the next-fastest evaluated multi-plane GPU baseline. FAST also demonstrates strong robustness to geometric noise and competitive single-plane detection, achieving 94.9% success on clean single-plane shapes.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
Reflection symmetry is a fundamental property of 3D shapes,
with applications in shape recognition and
reconstruction [ 29 ] .
Many objects exhibit multiple reflection planes, making
the recovery of all global symmetries an important geometric
task. However, detecting these planes accurately and
efficiently remains challenging, particularly for noisy
shapes and objects with many symmetries.

Our central insight is to treat the resulting geometric votes
as a signal over plane orientations, enabling efficient
processing through spherical harmonics.
We construct a continuous symmetry field by smoothing this
signal with a projective geodesic Gaussian kernel.
Crucially, this kernel is zonal, meaning that it depends only
on the relative orientation of two plane normals.
This allows us to exploit the Funk-Hecke theorem [ 30 ] , the spherical counterpart of
the Fourier convolution theorem for zonal kernels.
Just as the convolution theorem enables efficient filtering
through FFTs, Funk-Hecke transforms our Gaussian smoothing
operation into simple multiplication of harmonic coefficients.
Combined with fast spherical-harmonic transforms and synthesis,
this enables efficient construction and evaluation of the
symmetry field across densely sampled orientations.

blocks.en: 5 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 5 结论

blocks.en:
We presented FAST, a training-free framework for detecting
multiple global reflection symmetries in 3D shapes.
By treating geometric pair votes as a signal over plane
orientations, FAST exploits the Funk-Hecke theorem to
efficiently construct and evaluate a continuous symmetry
field in the spherical-harmonic domain.
Geometric screening, witness weighting, continuous refinement,
and verification turn this efficient representation into a
reliable symmetry detector.
Across two benchmarks, FAST achieves the highest clean
multi-plane detection accuracy among evaluated methods,
with GPU inference below 4 4 ms per shape, while
demonstrating strong noise robustness and competitive
single-plane performance.
These results establish harmonic voting as an efficient
alternative to costly geometric search and learned
symmetry detection.

方向, FAST 利用 Funk-Hecke 定理
高效构建和评估连续对称性
字段在球形-谐音域。
几何筛选、证人加权、不断改进、
核查将这种有效的代表性变成一种
可靠的对称探测器。
通过两个基准,FAST实现最高的清洁
评估方法中的多飞机探测准确性,
GPU 推论低于 4 4 ms 的每个形状,而
表现出强烈的噪音和竞争力
单机性能.
这些结果使口琴投票成为有效的
